Q: Stop Hibernate adding associations to SQL select when using legacy Criteria API? A:

This is default EAGER fetching behavior for @ManyToOne & @OneToOne relationships. The Criteria API respects the mapping level fetch configurations by default. but can you control this behavior explicitly with methods like SetFetchMode("Bids", FetchMode.Lazy) to disable eager fetching when needed.

Q: How would I find the column given a data-value in SQL? A:

the simplest way:

SELECT 
    STRING_AGG(COLUMN_NAME + ' = ''my-data-val''', ' OR ') AS where_clause
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'MRE_TABLE'

Q: PowerShell : how to zip directory based on file name A:

Replace the folder block in your original with this:

# --- Add every file inside the folder, preserving relative paths ---
$folderFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $folderPath -File -Recurse
foreach ($f in $folderFiles) {
    $relativePath = $f.FullName.Substring($sourceDir.Length).TrimStart('\','/')
    $entry  = $archive.CreateEntry($relativePath)
    $fileIn = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($f.FullName)
    $fileIn.CopyTo($entry.Open())
    $fileIn.Dispose()
}

And define $folderPath just before the try:

$folderPath = Join-Path $sourceDir $file.BaseName

Q: What is the difference between named and positional parameters in Dart? A:

In Dart, we have two types of parameters: Positional and Named parameters.

Positional Parameters
Required positional:

  • Declared normally.

  • Order is very important.

  • They cannot have default values.

void requiredPositionalOnly(double width, double length) {}

// Calls 
requiredPositionalOnly(); // Error: 2 arguments expected 
requiredPositionalOnly(2, 3); // OK

Optional positional:

  • Declared in square brackets, [].

  • Order is very important.

  • They can be omitted if non-nullable; otherwise, they must have a default value.

void optionalPositionalOnly([double? width, double length = 20]) {}
// Calls
optionalPositionalOnly();        // OK, uses defaults
optionalPositionalOnly(20, 30);  // overrides defaults

Positional arguments must always be passed in the declared order.

Named Parameters:

  • Declared in curly braces {}.

  • Arguments are passed by name, so order doesn't matter.

  • Can be optional (with a default value or nullable) or required (using required).


void optionalNamedOnly({double width = 10, required double length}) {}

// Calls
optionalNamedOnly(); //Error: 'length' is required
optionalNamedOnly(length: 5); // OK
optionalNamedOnly(length: 12, width: 15); // OK
optionalNamedOnly(23); // Error: must use names

Mixing Parameters:

  • You can combine required positional with either optional positional or named, but not both optional positional and named in the same signature.

  • Required positional always comes first


void withRequiredAndOptionalPositional(double width, [double height = 10]) {}
void withRequiredAndNamed(double width, {double length = 10, required double height}){}
